overview: Vaiyavritya, in Jainism, refers to the act of service or care provided to monks, nuns, and other members within the community. It is considered a significant form of lay practice and is highly encouraged as it supports the spiritual endeavors of ascetics, allowing them to focus on their spiritual pursuits without concerns for mundane necessities. Vaiyavritya encompasses various activities such as offering food, clothing, medicine, and other essential items needed by ascetics. This practice fosters a symbiotic relationship between the lay community and ascetics, reinforcing communal ties and spiritual advancement.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.notes: This sutra highlights the importance of offering service to ascetics as part of lay duties, emphasizing its role in spiritual development.

misconceptions.myth: Vaiyavritya is only about providing food to monks.
misconceptions.reality: Vaiyavritya includes a wide range of services beyond just food, such as providing clothing, medicine, and other necessities to support ascetics in their spiritual practices.
